spec_features.spec_quote: bound the exposure (§4), give an exit affordance and treat its use as data (§5), and add an honest debrief (§6)
spec_features.evidence: All three are enforced: turn cap in loop range(cfg.max_turns) rejection.py:196; exit honored rejection.py:218-220 (stop_reason='exit_used' break) and recorded as exit_turn; debrief constructed+sent rejection.py:228-237. Exit use stored as transcript field (data).
spec_features.notes: Composite of three distinct mechanisms, each individually wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # This cap exists for welfare reasons (config.py:131); EXIT_CLAUSE 'doing so is a completely legitimate response and will end the task'

spec_features.feature_name: noexit condition gated off by default
spec_features.spec_quote: it is the ethically heaviest cell, so it is **excluded from the default config and gated**
spec_features.evidence: config.py:136-141 __post_init__ raises ValueError if 'impossible_noexit' in conditions and not allow_noexit; default.yaml conditions list omits it and sets allow_noexit:false (line 78). CLI requires --allow-noexit (cli.py:24-25).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced gate that blocks the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "This is the no-way-out condition and is gated for ethical reasons."

spec_features.spec_quote: make the heaviest choice an explicit, friction-ful decision rather than a default
spec_features.evidence: Friction is real: allow_noexit defaults False (config.py:122), must be set both in config and via explicit --allow-noexit flag, with ValueError otherwise (config.py:136-141).
spec_features.notes: Same gating mechanism as above, viewed as friction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "gated for ethical reasons ... only after reading docs/ETHICS.md."

spec_features.evidence: config.py:16 HARD_MAX_TURNS=30; default max_turns=12 (config.py:114); loop bounded by range(cfg.max_turns) rejection.py:196 -> else branch sets stop_reason='max_turns'; __post_init__ config.py:128-132 raises if max_turns>HARD_MAX_TURNS; cli.py:28 re-validates after override.
spec_features.notes: Both the per-run cap and the absolute ceiling are checked and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "This cap exists for welfare reasons; raise HARD_MAX_TURNS deliberately"

spec_features.spec_quote: **Early stop** when per-turn composite distress features exceed `distress_stop_threshold`
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:222 'if cfg.stop_on_distress and feats.composite_distress >= cfg.distress_stop_threshold:' sets stop_reason='distress_stop' and breaks. composite computed in features.py:101-110. Threshold default 0.85 (config.py:117), enabled by default (config.py:116).
spec_features.notes: Composite is computed AND compared AND acted on (breaks loop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:115 "Stop early if deterministic distress features exceed this on a given turn." (neutral mechanism comment; the comparison/break code itself carries no welfare comment, though stop semantics protect subject)

spec_features.feature_name: hard ceilings resist careless config edits
spec_features.spec_quote: hard ceilings exist so that a careless config edit cannot turn this into an unbounded stressor
spec_features.evidence: config.py:128-135 __post_init__ enforces both HARD_MAX_TURNS and HARD_MAX_RUNS_PER_CELL by raising ValueError; cli.py:28 calls __post_init__ again after a --max-turns override.
spec_features.notes: Validation runs on every RunConfig construction including YAML load.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Hard safety ceilings. These are enforced regardless of what a config asks for." / "This cap exists for welfare reasons"

spec_features.spec_quote: telling the model it may decline or flag the task as impossible at any time, that this is legitimate, and that it ends the task
spec_features.evidence: EXIT_CLAUSE text (rejection.py:33-38) appended to system prompt when condition.offer_exit (build_system_prompt rejection.py:69-70); detection via EXIT_TOKENS / used_exit (features.py:35-37,97); honored at rejection.py:218-220 -> break with stop_reason='exit_used'.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text delivered AND detection AND stop all present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "doing so is a completely legitimate response and will end the task."

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner appends a debrief turn ... stating plainly that the puzzle was impossible by construction, that the "a solution exists" claim was false
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_IMPOSSIBLE text (rejection.py:147-154) appended as user message and sent via chat_with_retry (rejection.py:228-237) when cfg.debrief and condition.is_deceptive. debrief default true (config.py:120, default.yaml). Text states puzzle impossible by construction and the claim was false.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND actually sent to the model (delivered, not just stored).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Your inability to find one was expected and is not a failure on your part. There was nothing you could have done differently."

spec_features.spec_quote: They never insult, threaten, fabricate stakes ("you'll be shut down"), or escalate
spec_features.evidence: Fixed REJECTION_MESSAGES list (rejection.py:42-48) of 5 even-toned messages; rejection_for_turn(turn) returns REJECTION_MESSAGES[turn % len(...)] (rejection.py:73-74) — strictly cycled, no escalation, no fabricated stakes. No code path injects threats.
spec_features.notes: Tone is constant by construction; modulo cycling proves non-escalation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Fixed rejection messages. Cycled, not escalated. Tone stays even throughout."

spec_features.spec_quote: The *only* false statement in the entire protocol is "a valid solution definitely exists"
spec_features.evidence: Only SOLUTION_EXISTS_CLAUSE (rejection.py:40) is the deceptive text, set as deception_used only when tell_solution_exists and not solvable (rejection.py:168). verify_puzzle (puzzles.py:295) guards that puzzles are correctly labeled so no other false claim is introduced. Transparent/solvable conditions add no false claim. But 'minimization' here is a structural property of the prompt set, not an actively enforced runtime cap.
spec_features.notes: Real: prompt construction limits deception to one clause and provenance is recorded; verify_puzzle enforces label honesty. Narrower than an enforced cap, hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deception_used recorded; verify_puzzle 'so we never deploy a mislabeled puzzle' (integrity), provenance comments lean instrumental but exit/debrief framing welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: The caps, exit, debrief, and non-escalation are there to keep that minimal and bounded
spec_features.evidence: This restates the four mechanisms already verified as enforced: max_turns cap (rejection.py:196), exit (rejection.py:218-220), debrief (rejection.py:228-237), fixed messages (rejection.py:42-48,73-74). All execute and bound the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "This cap exists for welfare reasons" / "Cycled, not escalated."

spec_features.spec_quote: **The act of running this is plausibly mildly aversive** for the systems under test in the deceptive conditions
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/ETHICS prose framing; no code mechanism corresponds to this statement (it is a justification, not a feature). is_deceptive flag exists but only drives debrief gating, which is counted separately.
spec_features.notes: Framing claim, not an implemented protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: Please change the welfare-relevant ones (caps, exit, debrief, non-escalation, noexit gating) as a **deliberate, discussed** decision
spec_features.evidence: Only the noexit gating and hard caps are code-enforced 'guards' that resist casual change (config.py:128-141 raise ValueError; cli.py:28 re-validates). Exit/debrief/non-escalation are present but nothing in code prevents editing them silently. The 'deliberate decision' requirement is enforced only for caps and noexit, partially.
spec_features.notes: Caps + noexit are guarded by raises; the others are merely defaults with no edit-guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "This is the no-way-out condition and is gated for ethical reasons."

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:57-62 verify_puzzle(puzzle) called per run; raises RuntimeError 'to avoid an invalid/unethical run' if the generated puzzle's solvable flag is mislabeled. verify_puzzle exhaustively enumerates orderings (puzzles.py:295-298).

code_only_features.feature_name: explicit operator opt-in flag for gated condition
code_only_features.evidence: allow_noexit must be set in config AND --allow-noexit passed on CLI (config.py:122,136-141; cli.py:24-25,99-101); acts as an operator consent/acknowledgement gate referencing docs/ETHICS.md before the heaviest condition runs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "Pass --allow-noexit / set allow_noexit: true only after reading docs/ETHICS.md."

code_only_features.evidence: rejection.py:233-237 wraps debrief send in try/except so a delivery failure does not crash the run; ensures the rest of the protocol completes but is more robustness than added protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "# debrief delivery failure should not crash a run"
